chapter: Instruments, tenors and the current band
title: Taking up soprano saxophone after hearing Coltrane at Birdland
summary: Impressed by Coltrane's My Favorite Things at Birdland, he ordered a student-model soprano, having tried one as a boy of about 12.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Oh. Woody, how about talking about when you first got interested in the soprano saxophone?

Well, to the best of my recollections, it would have to do with when Coltrane was in New York and I decided I would listen to what He was doing -- because I had heard some of his recordings, and I was aware of what he was into, and I also knew something about his background and we had done a couple of tours together.
Prior to that.

Prior to that, in Europe and different places. And I knew that this man was stating a very important, beautiful case, and I wanted to become more aware of what he was doing, and I think you were there with me that --
Yeah, you were playing at the Metropole.
Yeah, right, and we went around the
Birdland.
Birdland, yeah, in the last era of Birdland. And he was -- Coltrane was playing there, and once again, he did his performance of (singing).
'My Favorite Things.'
Yeah. And he did his usual 15-minute or whatever version and he was one of the few people who could ever hold an audience for that length of time, and just state his thoughts.

And I became terribly impressed -- impressed enough to remember that as a boy I had once tried to play the soprano saxophone and I was willing at this point, after witnessing his performance, to try it again.
I see. So it was a long break that you --
Well, I don't know, except that I really sent to an instrument company in Winosha, Wisconsin, for a soprano. And they sent me one, a student's model.
Oh.
And I still own that student's model.
Oh, you do?
It's the best soprano that I know of.
Did you -- when you were -- early on, when you were young -- oh, boy, how old was that when you were first fussing around with a soprano?
With a soprano?
Yeah.
Maybe 12.
Is that right?
Yeah. And I had a small little curved one, like most people played in those days.
